meta.title: Spread spectrum and CDMA with Walsh and Gold-like codes
meta.tools: NumPy DS-CDMA simulator, Walsh–Hadamard and random spreading codes, Gaussian-approximation theory
meta.summary: Put K users on the same band with direct-sequence spreading: orthogonal Walsh codes (synchronous) give single-user BER; random codes (asynchronous-like) suffer multiple-access interference that follows the standard Gaussian approximation.
meta.problem: How can many users transmit on the same frequency at the same time, and what limits how many?
meta.theory:
Spreading factor N: each bit becomes N chips. With orthogonal codes (synchronous) cross-correlation is zero → BER = single-user
$Q(\sqrt{2E_b/N_0})$. With random codes, each interferer adds variance ≈ E_b/N per bit, so (standard Gaussian approximation)
$P_b\approx Q\!\left(\left[\frac{K-1}{N}+\frac{N_0}{2E_b}\right]^{-1/2}\right)$ — capacity is interference-limited.
meta.method:
N = 32 chips/bit, K = 1…24 users, equal power, E_b/N₀ = 8 dB, 20,000 bits per user per point. Walsh rows of a 32×32 Hadamard matrix vs
independent random ±1 sequences (redrawn each bit).

rows.quantity: Walsh codes: BER pooled over all K (should equal single-user BER)
rows.note: 140,000 bits pooled; each K alone has only ~4 expected errors
